newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says seeks to avoid US shortage after fire.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says seeks to avoid US shortage after fire.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Monday that it was trying to avoid a shortage of its cars in the United States after a fire at a parts supplier impeded Japanese production last week.
A company spokeswoman, however, declined to provide any estimate of the impact of the fire on exports.
"We resumed full operation of our domestic factories today and will increase production to catch up," said the spokeswoman.

The Asian Wall Street Journal said on Monday that an executive in Toyota's overseas division, who was not named, had estimated that Toyota will ship 10,000 fewer Camrys, RAV4s, 4-Runners and Lexus models to the United States than the 40,000 it had originally planned to ship in February.
The spokeswoman declined to comment on the report.

Last week, Toyota officials said in Chicago that the company's North American production had not been affected by the fire on February 1 at the parts supplier. They said there were enough parts en route to the United States and Canada to allow assembly plants there to operate for about a month.
